items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Nancy Wilson; the interviewer mentions her in the context of DownBeat magazine covers.

ctx.x: that was so influential in how I saw the guitar, which I credit to that moment of crossing paths with him. And then fast forward when I moved to New York and I hung out with him and took some lessons. And Gene was always so welcoming of me anytime I came by to sit in with him and introduce me to people. He was just so generous. But anyway, that’s what I studied with him was arranging standards. And I learned so much, I mean stuff that I share with all my students and stuff that I’m still working on all the time.

Um hum. There’s two topics that are often subjects of scholarly writings. One is jazz and race, and the other one that I’d like to bring up is women in jazz. And I found this in my stuff here — this is an issue of DownBeat December 1964. And I was looking through it and the only mention of a woman musician was a letter writer to the editor saying, “Nancy Wilson is beautiful.” Apparently they did have her on a previous cover. And he wrote in to say that that’s the best cover ever. So that was 1964. Now if we fast…
